content: Gemifloxacin is a medication used to treat various bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as quinolone antibiotics and is effective only against bacterial infections, not viral infections like the common cold or flu. How to Use: Before starting gemifloxacin, read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist, and review it again each time you get a refill. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. These include quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals (such as iron or zinc), and products containing magnesium or aluminum (e.g., antacids). For best results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Possible Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, headache, or difficulty sleeping. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, gemifloxacin may cause a severe intestinal condition due to the bacteria Clostridium difficile (C. diff), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Mild rashes are common and usually not serious, but it can be difficult to distinguish them from rare, severe allergic reactions. The risk of developing a rash is higher in individuals under 40 years old, women (especially those on hormone replacement therapy), or when the medication is taken for more than 7 days. Precautions: Before using gemifloxacin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other quinolone antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Gemifloxacin may rarely cause a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation), which can increase the risk of serious irregular heartbeats. The risk is higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood may also increase this risk, especially if caused by diuretics, severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may rarely cause significant changes in blood sugar levels, particularly in individuals with diabetes. Monitor your blood sugar regularly and report any symptoms of high blood sugar (e.g., increased thirst or urination) or low blood sugar (e.g., sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands/feet). Carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar, or use quick sources of sugar like honey, candy, fruit juice, or non-diet soda if needed. Inform your doctor immediately about any reactions. Gemifloxacin may make you dizzy, and alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Special Considerations: Gemifloxacin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). Children may be at greater risk for joint or tendon problems while using this drug. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk in small amounts, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not contain all possible drug interactions. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Storage: Store gemifloxacin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This summary does not include all possible information about gemifloxacin. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
